evaluations.question: Can you describe the RAG pipeline you built with ChromaDB and sentence‑transformers?
evaluations.answer: I built a FastAPI service with a RAG pipeline. I chunked the documents, embedded them with a sentence-transformers model and stored the vectors in ChromaDB, then retrieved the top chunks to ground the LLM prompt.
strengths: Mentions all core components (FastAPI, chunking, sentence‑transformers, ChromaDB, retrieval)
Shows understanding of the overall RAG flow
improvements: Provide more detail on chunk size, embedding model, and indexing method
Explain how the retrieved chunks are formatted into the LLM prompt
Mention any libraries (e.g., LangChain) or LLM integration specifics
evaluations.model_answer: In the FastAPI app I first split each document into overlapping chunks (e.g., 500‑token windows). Each chunk is encoded with a sentence‑transformers model (e.g., all‑MiniLM‑L6‑v2) to obtain a dense vector. The vectors are up‑serted into a ChromaDB collection, which builds an ANN index. At query time the user question is encoded with the same model, the index returns the top‑k most similar chunks, and those chunks are concatenated into a prompt that is sent to the LLM (e.g., Groq or OpenAI). The response is returned via the FastAPI endpoint. Optional steps include storing metadata, caching, and using LangChain prompt templates.
